parts.title: Learning by example
parts.subtitle: Evidence from studies of rats and birds
parts.article:
Learning by example

A The best known model of animal learning behaviour is probably the so-called classical model associated with the Russian scientist Pavlov. The key features of this model are stimulus, outcome and repetition. Pavlov demonstrated that animals could be trained to associate a sensory stimulus with a particular outcome, even where no natural association exists. In one famous experiment, dogs learned to associate the sound of a bell with the expectation of food. Subsequent models, such as the ‘operant conditioning’ model, also involved observing animals in isolation. Recently, however, behavioural research has focused on how animals are equipped to learn in social settings. And interest in the concept of role modelling, already a popular notion for guiding child development, has spread to other species.

B Heyes and Galef (1996) have compiled some very interesting and accessible papers on social learning in mammals. One of these papers starts with an account of a school field trip to Israel. In a pine forest there, many pine cones were discovered which had been stripped to the central core. So an investigation was started which had no weighty theoretical intent, but was directed initially at finding out what were eating the nutritious pine seeds, and how they managed to get them out of the cones. The culprit proved to be the versatile and athletic black rat. The forest-dwelling rat used a standard technique, biting off each cone scale in sequence, from base to tip, following the spiral growth pattern of the cone.

C The investigation was then broadened, with the aim of determining how the rat acquires such a skill. Urban black rats were found to lack the skill, and were unable to learn it even when they were housed with experienced cone strippers, such as those found in Israel. However, infants of urban mothers who were fostered to forest mothers acquired the skill, whereas infants of forest mothers fostered by urban mothers did not. Clearly, the skill is not inherited, but has to be taught.

D Further elegant experiments showed that naive adult urban rats can develop the skill if they are provided with cones from which the first complete spiral of scales have been removed, rather as people can deduce how to use a new photocopier once they have been shown how to switch it on. In the case of forest rats, mothers supply their infants with cones which they have partially stripped, thereby providing the key for acquiring the complete stripping skill.

E We might conclude that this is a good example of adaptive learning, but how economical is it? The researchers went on to determine this by measuring the oxygen uptake of a rat stripping a cone. The rat was placed in a metabolic chamber so that the amount of energy used in the cone-stripping operation could be calculated. This was then compared with the energy benefit of the pine seeds, as measured by a machine known as a calorimeter. The rat's energy expenditure proved to be less than 10% of the energetic value of the cone – an acceptable profit margin.

F A paper by Bednekoff and Balda (1996) provides another example of the adaptiveness of social learning, this time in birds. It concerns the seed caching behaviour of two birds: Clark's Nutcracker (Nucifraga columbiana) and the Mexican Jay (Aphelocoma ultramarina). The former is a specialist, caching 30,000 or so seeds in scattered locations, from where it recovers them over the winter months. The Mexican Jay also caches food, but is not nearly as dependent on this as the Nutcracker. The two species also differ in their social structure, the Nutcracker being rather solitary, while the Jay forages in social groups.

G An experiment was conducted to discover not just whether a bird can remember where it hid a seed itself, but also if it can remember where it saw another bird hide a seed. The design of the experiment is slightly comical, with a cacher bird wandering about a room with lots of holes in the floor and hiding food in some of them, while watched by an observer bird perched in a cage. Two days later, cachers and observers are tested for their discovery rate against an estimated random performance. In the role of cacher, not only the Nutcracker but also the less specialised Jay performed above the rate of chance. More surprisingly, however, Jay observers were as successful as Jay cachers, whereas Nutcracker observers did no better than chance. So it seems that, whereas the Nutcracker is highly adapted for remembering where it hid its own seed, the gregarious Mexican Jay is more adept than the Nutcracker at remembering, and so exploiting, the caches of other birds.

questions.question: an overview of research into learning behaviour in animals

你可能会觉得其他段落也在讲动物学习，但只有A段给出了整个研究发展历程的“宏观概述（overview）”。

questions.question: The purpose of the field trip to Israel was to investigate the feeding habits of the black rat.

analyses.content: 去以色列只是学校的实地考察，考察时偶然发现了被啃过的松果才开始调查并发现了黑鼠，而不是一开始就为了调查黑鼠的饮食习惯而去的。
你可能会因为看到原文提到了以色列和黑鼠就选TRUE，但搞错了事情发生的先后顺序和因果关系。

questions.question: Pine cones are the main source of food for forest rats in Israel.

analyses.content: 原文只提到了森林里的老鼠会吃松果里的松子，但完全没提这到底是不是它们“最主要的（main）”食物来源。
你可能会想当然地觉得老鼠费这么大劲吃松果肯定是因为这是主食，但做阅读题千万不能脑补原文没写的信息。

In a pine forest there, many pine cones were discovered which had been stripped to the central core. So an investigation was started which had no weighty theoretical intent, but was directed initially at finding out what were eating the nutritious pine seeds, and how they managed to get them out of the cones. The culprit proved to be the versatile and athletic black rat. The forest-dwelling rat used a standard technique, biting off each cone scale in sequence, from base to tip, following the spiral growth pattern of the cone.

questions.question: The forest rats in Israel had a fixed method of peeling pine cones.

analyses.content: 原文明确指出森林里的老鼠使用的是一种“标准的技巧”，从底到尖按固定顺序咬，完美对应题干的固定方法（fixed method）。
你可能会因为原文没一模一样地出现“fixed method”这个词而犹豫，其实“standard technique”就是最直接的同义替换。
The forest-dwelling rat used a standard technique, biting off each cone scale in sequence, from base to tip, following the spiral growth pattern of the cone.

questions.question: Forest rats know instinctively how to peel pine cones.

analyses.content: 原文斩钉截铁地说这项技能“不是遗传的（not inherited）”，必须靠后天教导，这直接反驳了题干说的老鼠“本能地（instinctively）”知道怎么剥松果。
你可能会不认识“instinctively”（本能地）或者“inherited”（遗传的），这两个词是完美的反义考点，一个是天生就会，一个是非天生的。

Urban black rats were found to lack the skill, and were unable to learn it even when they were housed with experienced cone strippers, such as those found in Israel. However, infants of urban mothers who were fostered to forest mothers acquired the skill, whereas infants of forest mothers fostered by urban mothers did not. Clearly, the skill is not inherited, but has to be taught.

questions.question: In extracting pine seeds from the cones, rats use only a small proportion of the energy they gain from eating them.

analyses.content: 原文说老鼠剥松果消耗的能量还不到吃掉松子所获能量的10%，这完美证实了题干中的“只使用获得能量的一小部分（a small proportion）”。
你可能会被前面复杂的实验过程绕晕，但只要紧盯最后一句“less than 10%”（不到10%）这个数据，就能稳稳确认答案。

groups.contentHtml:
Clark’s Nutcracker and the Mexican Jay
Clark’s Nutcracker and the Mexican Jay are two species of bird which store seeds in various places for use in winter. The Jay relies on this habit, and is more in its feeding habits. During an experiment, one bird stored seeds while another . Of the two species, the was consistently more able to find seeds which had been stored by other birds.

analyses.content: 原文直白地说墨西哥松鸦不像星鸦那样极度依赖（not nearly as dependent on）藏食物的习惯，也就是依赖得较少，对应选项G（less）。
你可能看到原文有“dependent”就想选C，但是忽略了前面的否定词和比较级“not nearly as... as”，导致意思截然相反。
The Mexican Jay also caches food, but is not nearly as dependent on this as the Nutcracker.
原文对比指出星鸦比较孤僻，而松鸦是群体觅食（in social groups），这对应了选项H（社会的/群居的）。
你可能会看到前半句写星鸦的“solitary”（孤独的）就误选E，但题目问的是“Jay”（松鸦）的习惯，找错对象就全错了。
The two species also differ in their social structure, the Nutcracker being rather solitary, while the Jay forages in social groups.
原文描述实验场景时明确说，一只鸟藏食物的时候，被另一只关在笼子里的观察鸟“看着（watched）”，空格需要动词，所以选D。
你可能看到选项有名词“observer”（F选项）就想往里填，但空格前是“another”（另一个），后面缺一个表示动作的谓语动词，填名词在语法上根本说不通。

The design of the experiment is slightly comical, with a cacher bird wandering about a room with lots of holes in the floor and hiding food in some of them, while watched by an observer bird perched in a cage.
结论部分明确指出，松鸦（Jay）在记住并利用其他鸟类藏的食物方面，比星鸦更在行，所以选I。
你可能会被长句里的来回对比绕晕，但只要抓住结论句末尾的“exploiting the caches of other birds”（利用其他鸟藏的食物）对应的主语是“Mexican Jay”，就不会张冠李戴。

More surprisingly, however, Jay observers were as successful as Jay cachers, whereas Nutcracker observers did no better than chance. So it seems that, whereas the Nutcracker is highly adapted for remembering where it hid its own seed, the gregarious Mexican Jay is more adept than the Nutcracker at remembering, and so exploiting, the caches of other birds.
